h: Pairing Murton with the rest of York
p: Murton Park makes a good counterweight to the busy heart of York. It sits just off the ring road to the east, so it's easy to pop out for a morning of farm history and fresh air before heading back into the city in the afternoon. Families with young children often find this kind of split works well, as the open space gives everyone room to breathe before tackling the narrow streets of the old town.

The site is well known for recreating different periods of history for school groups, so there may be reconstructions and costume sessions running on some days. Because of that, family visits can feel quite different depending on what's scheduled, which is why a quick check on opening and events is wise before you set off.

Back in the city, there's a near-endless list of things to do. The National Railway Museum, near the station, is a must for train fans and pairs perfectly with the little Derwent Valley Light Railway at Murton. JORVIK Viking Centre tells the story of the Viking city, and a walk round the medieval city walls gives you some of the best views of York Minster. The Shambles, with its overhanging timber buildings, is worth wandering early in the day before the crowds build.

If you'd rather stay out in the countryside, the villages and lanes east of York are pleasant for a drive, and the Yorkshire Wolds are within reach for rolling hills and big skies. Pack wellies and a waterproof for Murton, and save your comfy trainers for the city cobbles.
